library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

Carter et al. (2020) measured pitavastatin and eltrombopag together in
suspended human hepatocytes, described the uptake with a structurally
identifiable micro-rate-constant model, and scaled the estimates into a
semimechanistic PBPK model to predict the clinical interaction. The paper
contributes two models:

* `Carter_2020_pitavastatin_eltrombopag_invitro` -- the hepatocyte model
  (model 1 of Table 1: micro-rate constants, mutual competitive inhibition,
  both drugs measured).
* `Carter_2020_pitavastatin_eltrombopag_pbpk` -- the semimechanistic PBPK
  model of oral pitavastatin (1 mg) and eltrombopag (75 mg) in healthy adults.

```{r model-info}
mod_iv <- readModelDb("Carter_2020_pitavastatin_eltrombopag_invitro")
mod_pbpk <- readModelDb("Carter_2020_pitavastatin_eltrombopag_pbpk")
ui_iv <- rxode2::rxode(mod_iv)
ui_pbpk <- rxode2::rxode(mod_pbpk)
```

* Citation: `r ui_iv$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.12505>
* Supplements (open access, PMC7179958): the Supplemental Material (ODEs of all
  candidate in vitro models in Tables S1-S2 and of the PBPK model in Table S3)
  and the Model Codes archive (Monolix model files and data, and the deSolve
  PBPK script `PBPK_Model.r`).

# Population

**In vitro.** Cryopreserved human hepatocytes from one 10-donor pool
(BioIVT LiverPool lot LYB: 8 Caucasian, 1 African American and 1 Hispanic
donor) were suspended at 1e6 cells/mL in Leibovitz L15 medium at 37 C.
Hepatocytes were pre-incubated for 15 min with vehicle or 45 nmol/mL
eltrombopag (1.5e6 cells/mL); pitavastatin was then added at 0.3, 1, 3, 10, 30
or 100 nmol/mL, which diluted eltrombopag to 30 nmol/mL and the cells to
1e6 cells/mL, and the cells were sampled 0.25-30 min later by an oil-spin
separation. There were three experiments. Each concentration in each
experiment was fitted as an individual data set in Monolix (35 data sets).

**PBPK.** No clinical data were fitted. The model was assembled from the in
vitro estimates, scaled to a whole liver, plus literature physiology for an
83-kg adult male, and was compared with published single-dose profiles: 1 mg
pitavastatin (Prueksaritanont 2014, n = 8; plasma converted to blood with
blood:plasma 0.425) and 75 mg eltrombopag (Deng 2011). The paper's figures and
Table 3 come from 100 Monte-Carlo subjects.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Carter_2020_pitavastatin_eltrombopag_pbpk")()$population` (and
likewise for the in vitro model).

# Part 1: in vitro hepatocyte model

## Experimental design as an event table

The model holds amounts per 1e6 cells. Because the pre-incubation (45 nmol/mL
in 0.8 mL with 1.2e6 cells) and the incubation after pitavastatin addition
(30 nmol/mL in 1.2 mL with 1.2e6 cells) both hold 30 nmol of eltrombopag per
1e6 cells, the 15-min pre-incubation is simulated by a 30-nmol eltrombopag dose
into the medium at time 0, followed by the pitavastatin dose at 15 min. Time is
measured from the start of the eltrombopag pre-incubation, as in the paper's
figures (pitavastatin is always added at 15 min).

```{r iv-events}
pita_conc <- c(0.3, 1, 3, 10, 30, 100) # nmol/mL = nmol per 1e6 cells in 1 mL
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 15, by = 0.5), seq(15, 45, by = 0.25))))

make_iv <- function(id, pita, etm) {
  doses <- data.frame(
    id = id, time = 15, amt = pita, cmt = "medium", evid = 1L, dvid = NA_integer_
  )
  if (etm > 0) {
    doses <- rbind(
      data.frame(id = id, time = 0, amt = etm, cmt = "medium_eltrombopag", evid = 1L, dvid = NA_integer_),
      doses
    )
  }
  # The model has two endpoints (cellular pitavastatin and eltrombopag);
  # dvid = 1 attaches each observation row to the first, and both
  # concentrations are returned as columns on every row.
  obs <- data.frame(id = id, time = obs_times, amt = 0, cmt = "intracellular", evid = 0L, dvid = 1L)
  out <- rbind(doses, obs)
  out$pita_conc <- pita
  out$arm <- if (etm > 0) "With eltrombopag" else "Pitavastatin alone"
  out
}

iv_events <- bind_rows(
  lapply(seq_along(pita_conc), function(i) make_iv(i, pita_conc[i], 0)),
  lapply(seq_along(pita_conc), function(i) make_iv(10 + i, pita_conc[i], 30)),
  # Eltrombopag-only control (Figure 3, panel '0')
  make_iv(21, 0, 30) |> mutate(pita_conc = 0)
) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

# The in vitro model has no random effects and each id is a different
# experimental condition; rxode2 warns on every multi-subject solve without
# omega, so muffle that one warning only.
iv_sim <- withCallingHandlers(
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod_iv, events = iv_events, keep = c("pita_conc", "arm")),
  warning = function(w) {
    if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
      invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    }
  }
) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

## Mass balance and transporter conservation

Eltrombopag is not eliminated in the hepatocyte model, so the amount in medium,
transporter and cell must stay at the 30-nmol dose; the two transporter-bound
amounts can never exceed the total transporter. Both checks compare a solve
against an exact identity, so tight tolerances are appropriate.

```{r iv-mass-balance}
To <- exp(ui_iv$theta[["ltransporter_tot"]])
mb <- iv_sim |>
  filter(id > 10) |>
  mutate(
    etm_total = medium_eltrombopag + transporter_bound_eltrombopag + intracellular_eltrombopag,
    bound_total = transporter_bound + transporter_bound_eltrombopag
  )
stopifnot(
  max(abs(mb$etm_total - 30)) < 1e-4,
  min(mb$bound_total) >= -1e-9,
  max(mb$bound_total) <= To + 1e-9
)
summary(mb$bound_total / To)
```

At 30 nmol eltrombopag the transporter is mostly occupied by eltrombopag, which
is why the pitavastatin uptake falls so much in its presence.

## Figure 2: cellular pitavastatin with and without eltrombopag

```{r figure-2, fig.height = 6}
iv_sim |>
  filter(pita_conc > 0, time >= 15) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Ccell, colour = arm)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~pita_conc, scales = "free_y", labeller = label_both) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Pitavastatin alone" = "blue", "With eltrombopag" = "red")) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (min)", y = "Cellular pitavastatin (nmol/mL)", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 2 of Carter 2020 (typical-value curves)."
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r figure-2-table}
fig2_tab <- iv_sim |>
  filter(pita_conc > 0, time %in% c(20, 25, 45)) |>
  select(pita_conc, arm, time, Ccell) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = arm, values_from = Ccell) |>
  mutate(ratio = `With eltrombopag` / `Pitavastatin alone`)

fig2_tab |>
  mutate(across(c(`Pitavastatin alone`, `With eltrombopag`), ~ signif(.x, 3)), ratio = round(ratio, 2)) |>
  rename(
    "Pitavastatin (nmol/mL)" = pita_conc,
    "Time (min)" = time,
    "Alone (nmol/mL)" = `Pitavastatin alone`,
    "With eltrombopag (nmol/mL)" = `With eltrombopag`,
    "Ratio" = ratio
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Typical-value cellular pitavastatin concentrations.")

# The inhibition is overcome as the pitavastatin concentration rises
# (Figure 2, 10-100 nmol/mL): the with/without ratio at 25 min increases
# monotonically with the pitavastatin concentration.
r25 <- fig2_tab |> filter(time == 25) |> arrange(pita_conc) |> pull(ratio)
stopifnot(all(diff(r25) > 0), r25[1] < 0.5, r25[length(r25)] > 0.5)
```

The typical-value curves reproduce the features of Figure 2: a rise to a
maximum within about 10 min of pitavastatin addition and a slow decline from
intracellular metabolism, saturation of uptake at the higher concentrations,
and an inhibition by eltrombopag that is overcome as the pitavastatin
concentration rises. Read from the figure, the median individual fits at 25 min
are about 4.3, 12.5, 28, 68, 157 and 265 nmol/mL without eltrombopag and 1.5,
4.7, 13, 40, 110 and 210 nmol/mL with it; the typical-value curves are within
roughly 30 percent of the first set and 15-40 percent below the second (more
inhibition). Figure 2 shows medians of the per-data-set fits, each with its own
fitted initial eltrombopag amounts, which a single set of median parameters
does not reproduce exactly.

## Figure 3: cellular eltrombopag in the presence of pitavastatin

Figure 3 expresses cellular eltrombopag as a percentage of the eltrombopag-only
control.

```{r figure-3}
etm_ctrl <- iv_sim |> filter(id == 21) |> select(time, ctrl = Ccell_eltrombopag)
max_ctrl <- max(etm_ctrl$ctrl)
fig3 <- iv_sim |>
  filter(arm == "With eltrombopag") |>
  mutate(pct = 100 * Ccell_eltrombopag / max_ctrl)

ggplot(fig3, aes(time, pct)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~pita_conc, nrow = 1, labeller = label_both) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (min)", y = "Eltrombopag (percent of max control)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 3 of Carter 2020 (typical values; time from the start of pre-incubation)."
  ) +
  theme_bw()

fig3_end <- fig3 |> filter(time == 45) |> select(pita_conc, pct)
knitr::kable(
  fig3_end |> mutate(pct = round(pct, 1)) |>
    rename("Pitavastatin (nmol/mL)" = pita_conc, "Eltrombopag at 45 min (percent of control max)" = pct)
)
pct_at <- function(p) fig3_end$pct[fig3_end$pita_conc == p]
stopifnot(
  # No visible effect of low pitavastatin concentrations on eltrombopag ...
  abs(pct_at(0.3) - pct_at(0)) < 1,
  # ... and displacement that grows over 10-100 nmol/mL pitavastatin.
  pct_at(100) < pct_at(30), pct_at(30) < pct_at(10), pct_at(10) < pct_at(0)
)
```

The model reproduces the direction of Figure 3 -- eltrombopag is displaced from
the cells only at the higher pitavastatin concentrations -- but the
typical-value displacement at 100 nmol/mL (a few percent) is smaller than the
median fit in the figure (about 15 percent). Eltrombopag accumulates
mainly by passive entry (`k_fE` = 0.05 /min), which pitavastatin does not
inhibit.

## Derived macro-rate constants and PBPK scaling

Table 2 converts the micro-rate constants into Michaelis-Menten constants
(Eqs. 6-7) and whole-liver clearances (Eqs. 8-9), using 139e6 hepatocytes per g
liver (HPGL), a liver weight of 1695.6 g, 1 mL of medium per 1e6 cells, the
molecular weights 421.46 (pitavastatin) and 442 (eltrombopag), and an
extracellular-space correction of 469 mL x 1.08 g/mL.

```{r scaling}
th <- exp(ui_iv$theta[!grepl("^propSd|^vcell", names(ui_iv$theta))])
vcell <- ui_iv$theta[["vcell"]]
hpgl <- 139
lwt <- 1695.6
mw_p <- 421.46
mw_e <- 442
th_pbpk <- exp(ui_pbpk$theta)

scale_tab <- tibble::tribble(
  ~quantity, ~from_invitro, ~pbpk_value,
  "Vmax.up.P (ng/min/liver)", th[["ltransporter_tot"]] * th[["lktrans"]] * mw_p * hpgl * lwt, th_pbpk[["lvmax"]],
  "Km.up.P (ng/mL)", (th[["lkoff"]] + th[["lktrans"]]) / th[["lkon"]] * 1 * mw_p, th_pbpk[["lkm"]],
  "Vmax.up.E (ng/min/liver)", th[["ltransporter_tot"]] * th[["lktrans_eltrombopag"]] * mw_e * hpgl * lwt, th_pbpk[["lvmax_eltrombopag"]],
  "Km.up.E (ng/mL)", (th[["lkoff_eltrombopag"]] + th[["lktrans_eltrombopag"]]) / th[["lkon_eltrombopag"]] * 1 * mw_e, th_pbpk[["lkm_eltrombopag"]],
  "Pdif.P (mL/min/liver)", th[["lkpass_in"]] * 1 * hpgl * lwt, th_pbpk[["lps_in"]],
  "Pdif.E (mL/min/liver)", th[["lkpass_in_eltrombopag"]] * 1 * hpgl * lwt, th_pbpk[["lps_in_eltrombopag"]],
  "Pdef.P (mL/min/liver)", th[["lkpass_out"]] * vcell * hpgl * (lwt - 469 * 1.08), th_pbpk[["lps_out"]],
  "Pdef.E (mL/min/liver)", th[["lkpass_out_eltrombopag"]] * vcell * hpgl * (lwt - 469 * 1.08), th_pbpk[["lps_out_eltrombopag"]]
) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (pbpk_value - from_invitro) / from_invitro)

scale_tab |>
  mutate(across(c(from_invitro, pbpk_value), ~ signif(.x, 4)), pct_diff = round(pct_diff, 1)) |>
  rename(
    "Quantity" = quantity,
    "Scaled from Table 2 micro-rate constants" = from_invitro,
    "Value in the PBPK model" = pbpk_value,
    "Difference (percent)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Whole-liver PBPK constants re-derived from the in vitro estimates.")

# The transporter constants reproduce the PBPK values within rounding (the
# script used 0.302 nmol/min and 22.6 nmol/mL for the pitavastatin Vmax and Km).
stopifnot(all(abs(scale_tab$pct_diff[1:4]) < 3))
```

The transporter constants agree within rounding. Three passive constants
differ, and the PBPK model keeps the values of the authors' script (see
Assumptions and deviations): P_dif.P = 117.8 mL/min corresponds to
k_fP = 5.0e-4 /min rather than the Table 2 median 5.5e-4 /min; P_def.E =
307 mL/min corresponds to k_bE = 0.62 /min (inside the Table 2 range 0.35-0.65
but not the median 0.43); and P_dif.E = 11784 mL/min is the Eq. 8 value, where
Table 2 and the Discussion print 1.2e5.

# Part 2: PBPK model

## Virtual subjects

The authors drew 100 subjects once and used the same subjects in every
scenario: each parameter is `rnorm(n, mean, sd = CV * mean)`. The model encodes
this as `theta * (1 + eta)` with `eta ~ N(0, CV^2)`. The etas are drawn here
with R's own generator, so the cohort is identical on every machine, and are
passed to every scenario through `params`.

```{r pbpk-cohort}
n_sub <- 100
om <- ui_pbpk$omega
set.seed(20200305)
etas <- as.data.frame(
  sapply(colnames(om), function(nm) rnorm(n_sub, 0, sqrt(om[nm, nm])), simplify = FALSE)
)
# Factors (1 + eta) at or below zero would give a non-positive parameter. With
# the CVs used (at most 30 percent) such a draw is a >3.3-SD event.
stopifnot(min(1 + as.matrix(etas)) > 0)
etas$id <- seq_len(n_sub)

dose_pita <- 1e6 # 1 mg in ng
dose_etm <- 75e6 # 75 mg in ng
t_pita <- seq(0, 400, by = 1) # min, as in the script
t_etm <- seq(0, 10800, by = 5) # min (180 h)

make_pbpk <- function(arm, pita, etm, times) {
  d <- NULL
  if (pita) d <- rbind(d, data.frame(time = 0, amt = dose_pita, cmt = "stomach", evid = 1L))
  if (etm) d <- rbind(d, data.frame(time = 0, amt = dose_etm, cmt = "stomach_eltrombopag", evid = 1L))
  obs <- data.frame(time = times, amt = 0, cmt = "central", evid = 0L)
  one <- rbind(d, obs)
  out <- merge(data.frame(id = seq_len(n_sub)), one)
  out$arm <- arm
  out[order(out$id, out$time, -out$evid), ]
}

solve_arm <- function(ev) {
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod_pbpk, events = ev, params = etas, keep = "arm", atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-10) |>
    as.data.frame()
}

sim_pita <- solve_arm(make_pbpk("Pitavastatin alone", TRUE, FALSE, t_pita))
sim_etm <- solve_arm(make_pbpk("Eltrombopag alone", FALSE, TRUE, t_etm))
sim_both <- solve_arm(make_pbpk("Both", TRUE, TRUE, sort(unique(c(t_pita, t_etm)))))
```

## Figure 4: simulated profiles

The script summarises each scenario by the mean profile and the 5th and 95th
percentile profiles of the 100 subjects (labelled "95% confidence intervals"
in the paper).

```{r figure-4-data}
summ_prof <- function(d, conc) {
  d |>
    group_by(time) |>
    summarise(
      mean = mean(.data[[conc]]),
      q05 = quantile(.data[[conc]], 0.05),
      q95 = quantile(.data[[conc]], 0.95),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}
prof <- bind_rows(
  summ_prof(sim_pita, "Cc") |> mutate(panel = "(a) Pitavastatin alone"),
  summ_prof(sim_both |> filter(time <= 400), "Cc") |> mutate(panel = "(b) Pitavastatin + eltrombopag"),
  summ_prof(sim_etm, "Cc_eltrombopag") |> mutate(panel = "(c) Eltrombopag alone"),
  summ_prof(sim_both |> filter(time %in% t_etm), "Cc_eltrombopag") |> mutate(panel = "(d) Eltrombopag + pitavastatin")
)
```

```{r figure-4ab}
prof |>
  filter(grepl("^\\((a|b)\\)", panel)) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 60)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = mean), colour = "blue") +
  geom_line(aes(y = q05), linetype = 2, colour = "blue") +
  geom_line(aes(y = q95), linetype = 2, colour = "blue") +
  facet_wrap(~panel) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Blood pitavastatin (ng/mL)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 4a-b of Carter 2020 (mean and 5th-95th percentile profiles, 100 subjects)."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r figure-4cd}
prof |>
  filter(grepl("^\\((c|d)\\)", panel), time > 0) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 60)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = mean), colour = "red") +
  geom_line(aes(y = q05), linetype = 2, colour = "red") +
  geom_line(aes(y = q95), linetype = 2, colour = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~panel) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(10, 30000)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Plasma eltrombopag (ng/mL)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 4c-d of Carter 2020 (mean and 5th-95th percentile profiles, 100 subjects)."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

## PKNCA on the mean profiles (Table 3)

Table 3 reports Cmax, tmax and AUC from time 0 to the last time point
(400 min for pitavastatin, 180 h for eltrombopag) of the **mean** profile. The
same quantities are computed here with PKNCA from the mean profiles above. The
eltrombopag values of Table 3 are given in ug/mL and are converted to ng/mL for
the comparison.

```{r pknca}
mean_prof <- prof |>
  transmute(
    treatment = sub("^\\([a-d]\\) ", "", panel),
    id = 1L,
    time = time / 60,
    conc = mean
  )

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(mean_prof, conc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_df <- mean_prof |>
  distinct(treatment, id) |>
  mutate(
    time = 0,
    amt = ifelse(grepl("^Pitavastatin", treatment), dose_pita, dose_etm)
  )
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  treatment = unique(mean_prof$treatment),
  start = 0,
  end = ifelse(grepl("^Pitavastatin", unique(mean_prof$treatment)), 400 / 60, 180),
  cmax = TRUE,
  tmax = TRUE,
  auclast = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~cmax, ~tmax, ~auclast,
  "Pitavastatin alone", 23.1, 0.97, 49,
  "Pitavastatin + eltrombopag", 47.8, 1.2, 119,
  "Eltrombopag alone", 10.6 * 1000, 5.2, 338 * 1000,
  "Eltrombopag + pitavastatin", 10.6 * 1000, 5.2, 339 * 1000
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", tmax = "h", auclast = "h*ng/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = "Mean-profile NCA vs. the PBPK rows of Carter 2020 Table 3. * differs by >20%."
)
```

```{r ddi-ratio}
res <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "auclast")) |>
  select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)
auc_ratio_pita <- res$auclast[res$treatment == "Pitavastatin + eltrombopag"] /
  res$auclast[res$treatment == "Pitavastatin alone"]
auc_ratio_etm <- res$auclast[res$treatment == "Eltrombopag + pitavastatin"] /
  res$auclast[res$treatment == "Eltrombopag alone"]
c(pitavastatin_auc_ratio = auc_ratio_pita, eltrombopag_auc_ratio = auc_ratio_etm)
stopifnot(
  # Table 3 PBPK R value 2.4 (2.2-3) for pitavastatin and 1 for eltrombopag.
  auc_ratio_pita > 2, auc_ratio_pita < 3,
  abs(auc_ratio_etm - 1) < 0.02
)
```

The packaged model reproduces the PBPK predictions of Table 3: pitavastatin
Cmax and AUC roughly double with eltrombopag (AUC ratio
`r round(auc_ratio_pita, 2)` vs. 2.4 in the paper), whereas pitavastatin has
no effect on eltrombopag (ratio `r round(auc_ratio_etm, 3)`). Monte-Carlo
draws differ from the authors', so the mean-profile values differ slightly from
Table 3. As the paper notes, the simulated eltrombopag AUC is more than twice
the clinical value (145 h ug/mL in Deng 2011) and its tmax later
(2.5 h observed), while the pitavastatin-alone Cmax is lower than the observed
38.8 ng/mL; these are properties of the published model, not of this
implementation.

## Typical-value profiles

```{r typical}
typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod_pbpk, "omega"),
  events = make_pbpk("Both", TRUE, TRUE, t_pita) |> filter(id == 1),
  atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-10
) |> as.data.frame()
typ_alone <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod_pbpk, "omega"),
  events = make_pbpk("Pitavastatin alone", TRUE, FALSE, t_pita) |> filter(id == 1),
  atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-10
) |> as.data.frame()
c(
  typical_cmax_alone = max(typ_alone$Cc),
  typical_cmax_with_eltrombopag = max(typ$Cc)
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Published code followed where it differs from the paper.** The PBPK model
  follows the authors' deSolve script `PBPK_Model.r` (Model Codes supplement),
  which produced Figure 4 and Table 3. With the values and equations as printed
  in Table 2 and Table S3 the model does not reproduce Table 3 (the typical
  pitavastatin Cmax falls to about 0.5 ng/mL), whereas with the script it does.
  The differences, each resolved in favour of the script:
  * Pitavastatin urinary loss is `Q_K * CL_ur.P * f_u.bl.P * C_blood` in the
    script; Eq. S46 prints `Q_K * CL_urine.P * S6` without the unbound fraction.
  * P_dif.E is 11784 mL/min in the script (= k_fE x 1 mL x 139 x 1695.6, Eq. 8);
    Table 2 and the Discussion print 1.2e5.
  * f_u.L.P is 0.02 in the script; Table 2 prints 0.026.
  * V_ext.H is 556 mL in the script (Watanabe 2009); Table 2 prints 469 mL
    (469 mL is still used inside the P_def scaling, Eq. 9).
  * CL_ur.P is 11.5 mL/min (Table 2: 12), P_dif.P 117.8 (118), P_def.P 104.2
    (104) and k_bile 0.0618 /min (0.062): rounding only.
  * Eltrombopag passes through the stomach with the shared gastric emptying
    rate k_ge in the script; Eq. S47 starts eltrombopag in the GI tract. Table 2
    lists k_ge for both drugs.
* **Scaling inputs that are not the Table 2 medians.** The script's P_dif.P
  (117.8 mL/min) corresponds to k_fP = 5.0e-4 /min and its P_def.E (307 mL/min)
  to k_bE = 0.62 /min, not to the Table 2 medians 5.5e-4 and 0.43 /min. Eq. 10
  prints CL_met.P with a division by f_u.L.P, but the tabulated 93 mL/min
  (`0.22 x 0.003 x 139 x 1695.6 x 0.6`) has none. The PBPK model uses the
  tabulated and scripted values; the in vitro model uses the Table 2 medians.
* **Monte-Carlo variability as eta.** The script samples every PBPK parameter
  from a normal distribution with a 10-30 percent CV. The model encodes this as
  `theta * (1 + eta)`, `eta ~ N(0, CV^2)`, all fixed. These are assumed, not
  estimated, variabilities. The script shares one gastric emptying rate,
  gallbladder volume and emptying rate, liver volumes and hepatic blood flow
  between the two drugs of a subject, and so does the model.
* **Eltrombopag Fa x Fg = 1 and f_u.pl.E = 0.005** were chosen by the authors
  by visual fit to the clinical eltrombopag data (Methods); they are carried
  as published.
* **Body size.** The main text scales to an 83-kg adult male; the title of
  Table S3 states 70 kg. The parameters are whole-body values, so the model
  has no weight covariate.
* **In vitro: no variance or residual-error magnitudes.** Monolix used
  log-normal parameters and a proportional residual error, but Table 2 reports
  only the median individual estimate and its range. The in vitro model is a
  typical-value model with the proportional residual SDs fixed at 0.
* **In vitro: initial eltrombopag amounts.** The authors fitted the eltrombopag
  amounts at the time of pitavastatin addition as free parameters per data set
  and do not report them. Here they are generated by simulating the 15-min
  pre-incubation with the model itself (30 nmol per 1e6 cells), which is how
  the authors obtained their starting values before freeing them. This is one
  reason the typical-value curves differ from the medians of the individual
  fits in Figures 2 and 3.
* **In vitro cell volume.** The observation uses V_cell = 0.003 mL (3 uL per
  1e6 cells, Methods); the Monolix code multiplies by 333, a 0.1 percent
  difference.
* **Supplement typographical error.** Eqs. S9 and S14 print the intracellular
  pitavastatin efflux as `k_bA`; the Monolix code uses k_bP (`k31`), as here.
* No erratum or correction notice for this article was found in Europe PMC
  (checked 2026-11-27).
